source: derived from the annex C generator, preset and bit order
note: The Proximity-1 CRC-32: generator 0x00a00805, zero preset, most-significant bit first, no reflection and no final inversion. The zero preset is what makes the empty and all-zero cases zero, and it is why a correct codeword has a zero syndrome.

encode.name: ascii-123456789
encode.note: The ASCII string "123456789" gives 0x51693c0c under generator 0x00a00805 with a zero preset.

encode.name: empty-input-is-zero
encode.note: The register starts at zero and is never clocked, so the result is zero. Follows from the zero preset.

encode.name: single-zero-octet-stays-zero
encode.note: A zero octet against a zero register produces no feedback at any of the eight steps, so the register stays zero. This is the case that distinguishes a zero preset from an all-ones one: it shares its expected octets with empty-input-is-zero deliberately, because an implementation that presets to all ones fails this one and passes neither.

encode.name: deadbeef
encode.note: The four octets de ad be ef give 0x4440d14c.
